info.title: PiglorOS Gateway
info.description: Canonical v1 contract for the local Gateway. The current contract version is 1.0.0-draft. Every failure is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body whose `code` is registered in `problem-types.json`. That registry is open: a later v1 revision may add a problem type, so a client handles an unknown `code` by its HTTP status and `retryable`; a registered code is never removed or renamed within v1. Every retry-safe mutation carries an `Idempotency-Key`. Events are ordered by Timeline sequence, never wall time. Response schemas are closed so this revision detects drift; clients must ignore unknown members because later v1 revisions may add optional members. No operation creates a real-world effect. Operations marked `x-pigloros-status: draft` are not registered by the current Gateway router; their golden examples validate contract shape only. `x-pigloros-limits` states request and response limits and how a served limit may move within v1. The API major is the first path segment; another major and unknown required schema or Event versions fail closed. The frozen served-operation baseline and its compatibility window are recorded in `compatibility/baseline.json`. Within v1, changes must follow the baseline rules: add optional members or accept more request values, but do not weaken response guarantees, change schema identity or change declared unknown-member handling. Open request objects ignore unknown members, closed request objects reject them, and a schema-less value such as `EventView.payload` is preserved verbatim.

get.description: Read the authenticated Principal's own session: its entities, the effective grants the host derives from its recorded authority, its consent, the current execution mode with the operator network grants and the Principal's network posture, and the EPF1 execution profile. Nothing is echoed from the request: the acting entity only selects the decision. The read is protected like every other operation: the Local Principal's grant must cover `session.read` for the acting entity.

post.description: Create revision 1 of a Scenario Room from a declarative descriptor. The server assigns the room ID and correlation ID, sorts the lists canonically, resolves each plugin against the host catalogue, computes `rule_set_hash` from canonical JSON rules and `descriptor_hash` from the canonical descriptor members, and derives `plugin_composition_hash` from the host catalogue. The decision requires `scenario-room.create` for the acting entity and covers every `persona` participant as an actor; `governance_ref` must name the host's governance record.

post.description: Admit one inert Decision Preview under the `decision-preview.create` grant: the `pigloros.match-score.v1` Recommendation of the acting entity's own Preference and OptionSpec revisions in an exact Scenario Room revision, under one installed EPF1. The order is: a malformed body, a missing or malformed `Idempotency-Key`, a malformed ULID and a `schema_version` that is not the integer 1 (`400`: `unsupported-version` for any other number), an oversized body (`413`) and another content type (`415`) before the authority decision; then the decision; then the Principal's in-flight slot (`429`, four at a time, exact retries included); then the claim lookup: the same key with another request is `409 idempotency-conflict`, and an exact retry re-checks the bound room's consent, finishes an interrupted attempt and answers the original `202` receipt bytes. A fresh request then passes the profile gate (`409 incompatible-profile` for a profile outside the bound mode's servable set or without an installed EPF1; the current release composition has no installed EPF1, so every fresh request stops here), the room (its `provenance.digest` must be `scenario_room.digest`), the bindings (`404`) and the room consent (`403`), and commits one `preview.request.v1` claim and its `preview.result.v1` result on the host-owned `decision-previews` Timeline in one store command, under the per-minute quota and the store ceiling (`429`). The `202` receipt names the preview: `request_id` = `operation_id` = the preview ID, the claim Event's ID. It never claims that anything committed: `getDecisionPreview` reports the state.

202.description: Admitted and computed (or the original admission of an exact retry, the same bytes). The receipt never claims that an Event committed.

400.description: `invalid-request` (a malformed body or ULID, a `schema_version` that is not a number, or a missing or malformed `Idempotency-Key`) or `unsupported-version` (a `schema_version` that is any number other than the integer 1), before the authority decision.

401.description: `unauthenticated`: the host has no Local Principal, or the request names no actor.

403.description: `unauthorized`, `consent-invalid` or `revoked`: the grant, or the bound room's `privacy_export_ref` consent, checked under the operation's permit. The consent is checked before an exact retry is answered, so a retry after the consent was revoked is `403 revoked`.

404.description: `not-found-or-unavailable`: a room, Preference or OptionSpec revision that is unknown, foreign (not the acting entity's), digest-mismatched or erased, or an acting entity that is not a `persona` participant of the room. Every case answers alike.

413.description: `resource-limit-exceeded`: the request body exceeds the Gateway body bound.

429.description: `resource-limit-exceeded`. Retryable without `Retry-After`: the Principal already has four requests in flight (`principal_concurrent_operations`), or the store executor is saturated. Retryable with `Retry-After`: the Principal used its per-minute admissions (`principal_admissions_per_minute`) until the window closes, or the caller or the host reached its denial-record bound. Permanent and not retryable: the store holds `decision_previews_per_store` previews.

500.description: `internal-safe-failure`: the store is inconsistent, in which case nothing is appended or recorded; or the result append failed after the claim committed for a reason other than an unavailable host, in which case the claim stays and an exact retry with the same key finishes the preview.

503.description: `temporarily-unavailable`. Retryable: the host cannot vouch for its revocation state, record the denial evidence or reach its store, including a result append that failed after the claim committed because the host could not answer (erasure containment unavailable, a stale execution-mode binding); the claim stays and an exact retry with the same key finishes the preview. Not retryable: the first preview of a store with an active erasure request on a Gateway without a Local erasure composition.

get.description: Observe one of the acting entity's own Decision Previews under the `decision-preview.read` grant. An unknown `preview_id` and a preview of another Principal or actor answer the same `404`. The bound room's consent is re-checked on every read. The state is `admitted` (no result yet), `committed`, `failed` (with its typed `failure.code`) or `degraded`: a computed preview whose Preference or OptionSpec revision was erased later withholds `/recommendation` with reason `deleted`. A committed Recommendation is recomputed from the bound revisions under `pigloros.match-score.v1`; `uncertainty` and `calibration` are `unavailable`.

parameters.description: The acting entity; the Local Principal's grant must cover it. Only its own previews are found. Without it the read is `401 unauthenticated`.

post.description: Revoke one of the acting Principal's own consents, named by the `EventId` of its `consent.granted.v1` Event (`consent_ref`), as the Principal's `Session` lists it. The revocation is one `consent.revoked.v1` Event on the Principal's consent Timeline; its sequence is the consent Timeline fence. It is recorded after every protected operation admitted before it completes and takes effect before the next decision: from then on every operation the consent governs is `403 revoked`, while the operations no consent governs (among them reading the Session and revoking a consent) stay available. Revocation stops future protected work; it is distinct from erasure and deletes nothing. It is monotonic: revoking a revoked consent returns its original revocation (`200`). The operation itself requires the `consent.revoke` grant like any protected operation.

post.description: Request the erasure of the acting subject's own data in one destruction-eligible scope class, under the `erasure.request` grant. The subject is the Local Principal acting as `x-piglor-actor-entity`; its data is the root Timelines the actor created and their Forks. The operation is consent-exempt. A malformed body, a body whose `impact_acknowledged` is not `true` and a missing or malformed `Idempotency-Key` are `400 invalid-request` before the authority decision; after the decision a scope class the deployment always retains is `400 erasure-scope-retained`. The `202` admission receipt names the erasure (`request_id` = `operation_id` = the `erasure_id`, derived from the Principal, the actor and the key), the BLAKE3 digest of the key, and binds the policy, the trust bundle and the execution-mode profile of the submission; an exact retry answers the same receipt bytes, also after a restart, a bundle rotation or a mode migration. The receipt never claims that anything was erased: `getErasure` reports the progress. A Gateway without a Local erasure composition answers `503`, and while the operator has closed erasure admissions a fresh request is `503 erasure-admissions-closed`.

parameters.name: x-piglor-actor-entity
parameters.description: The acting entity; the Local Principal's grant must cover it. It names the subject whose data is erased. Without it the request is `401 unauthenticated`.

202.description: Admitted (or the original admission of an exact retry). The receipt never claims that anything was erased.

400.description: `invalid-request` (a malformed body, `impact_acknowledged` not `true`, or a missing or malformed `Idempotency-Key`), `erasure-scope-retained` (a scope class the deployment always retains, answered after the authority decision) or `erasure-scope-too-large` (the subject's closure exceeds `erasure_closure_targets`; nothing was requested).

401.description: `unauthenticated`: the host has no Local Principal, or the request names no actor.

403.description: `unauthorized` (no grant covers the actor and `erasure.request`) or `revoked` (the Principal's grant was revoked or expired).

409.description: `idempotency-conflict` (the `Idempotency-Key` named another scope), `incompatible-profile`, or `erasure-quota-exhausted` (the subject used its lifetime share of `erasure_store_requests`; not retryable).

413.description: `resource-limit-exceeded`: the request body exceeds the Gateway body bound.

429.description: `resource-limit-exceeded`. Retryable without `Retry-After` while another erasure of the subject has not reached its first receipt or has an active attempt (one active erasure per subject); retryable with `Retry-After` when the caller or the host reached its denial-record bound for the current window.

503.description: `erasure-admissions-closed`: the operator closed new erasure admissions with `piglor-gateway erasure-admissions close` (not retryable; an exact retry of an admitted request is still answered). `temporarily-unavailable`: the Gateway serves no Local erasure, or its trust admission has expired, so new erasures are closed (both not retryable); or the host cannot vouch for its revocation state, record the denial evidence or reach its erasure store (retryable).

get.description: Observe one of the acting subject's own erasures under the `erasure.read` grant. The operation is consent-exempt. An unknown `erasure_id`, another subject's, a refused authority decision (which is recorded like any denial, or counted in its window's marker once over the denial-record bound) and a Gateway without a Local erasure composition all answer the same `404 not-found-or-unavailable`; it never enumerates.

parameters.name: x-piglor-actor-entity
parameters.description: The acting entity; the Local Principal's grant must cover it. Only its own erasures are found. Without it the read is `401 unauthenticated`.

401.description: `unauthenticated`: the host has no Local Principal, or the request names no actor.

404.description: `not-found-or-unavailable`: identical for an unknown id, another subject's id and a refused decision, including one over the denial-record bound; it never enumerates.

429.description: `resource-limit-exceeded` (retryable, without `Retry-After`): the store executor is saturated. A refused read past the denial-record bound answers the `404` instead.

500.description: `internal-safe-failure`: the erasure was admitted under an execution-mode profile this Gateway does not compile.

503.description: `temporarily-unavailable` (retryable): the host cannot vouch for its revocation state, record the denial evidence, or read the erasure.

EventCursor.description: An opaque continuation cursor bound to one Timeline and one host inventory generation. Clients pass it back unchanged; a cursor of an older generation is `append-conflict`.

IdempotencyKey.description: A caller-generated key of 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters. Repeating the key with the same request bytes returns the original result; reusing it with different bytes is `idempotency-conflict`.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem details body. `code` is the stable family of problem-types.json; `type` is its URN. `detail` is safe human-readable text whose wording is not part of the contract.

instance.description: The matched route template of the failed request; the request path only for an unrouted request.

retryable.description: Whether an identical retry may succeed later.

EventView.description: A committed Event. `seq` is its position in Timeline Order and is the commit receipt; `event_type` names its schema.

payload.description: The decoded payload when the canonical CBOR is JSON-compatible; absent otherwise.

EventPage.description: One page of committed Events in ascending Timeline Order. `next_from_seq` is null only when the Timeline is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null when the host binds no inventory generation.

WorldActionV1.description: The typed `world.action.v1` proposal. `params` are two JSON floats (X, Z, metres per second); integers are rejected at admission as `admission-rejected` (JSON Schema cannot distinguish them).

ActionRequest.description: One typed simulated action. It affects simulation state only; no route creates a real-world effect.

OwnTracksLocation.description: An OwnTracks `location` message; every other member is discarded by minimization.

AdmissionReceipt.description: The 202 answer of an asynchronous admission, such as `requestErasure`. It names the admitted request and the inputs it binds, and never claims that anything committed or was erased: the resource at `operation_url` reports the progress.

idempotency_key_digest.description: BLAKE3 of the idempotency key; the raw key is never echoed.

bound_inputs.description: The digests of the input revisions and profile the admission binds.

CommittedEventReceipt.description: The authoritative commit receipt: the Event at its Timeline sequence and the cursor that observes its Projection.

Digest.description: A BLAKE3-256 digest in lower-case hex.

PageCursor.description: An opaque resumable cursor. Clients pass it back unchanged; a cursor of another resource, generation or inventory is `append-conflict`.

DomainKey.description: A canonical lower-case ASCII identifier (so its length in characters is its length in bytes): a capability, dimension, Plugin, rule or option key.

Label.description: Participant-authored display text without control characters. Its UTF-8 encoding is at most 128 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.label_bytes`, enforced at admission); `maxLength` is the coarse character bound that follows from it.

ExecutionProfileId.description: An execution-profile family identifier: a versioned lower-case slug outside the `gateway-mode-` namespace of `GatewayModeProfileId`. The set is open, so clients handle unknown identifiers as unknown profiles. Allowed v1 identifiers are `replay-v1`, `deterministic-local-v1`, `deterministic-air-gapped-v1`, `live-local-v1` and `live-air-gapped-v1`. A Local deployment never reports an Air-Gapped profile.

ExecutionProfile.description: The EPF1 execution profile a resource was produced under, or its explicit absence. It does not carry the serving mode, which is `mode_profile`. Every Gateway resource reports `state: unavailable` with `reason: not-installed`, except a Decision Preview, which reports the EPF1 it was admitted under. The current release composition has no installed EPF1, so fresh preview requests fail with `409 incompatible-profile`. When `installed`, `profile_id` is the execution-profile family and `profile_digest` is the raw EPF1 digest. `profile_id` is always in the servable set of the resource mode.

state.description: `installed` or `unavailable`. The set is deliberately closed in v1.

reason.description: Why no EPF1 is reported. Open within v1; server invariant: `not-installed` is the only reason the Gateway emits.

GatewayModeProfileId.description: A Gateway execution-mode profile. Its `gateway-mode-` namespace is disjoint from the `ExecutionProfileId`: neither is ever accepted where the other is expected. The profiles are composition-verified, never installed, qualified or a reproducibility claim; their public declaration is `execution-mode-profiles.json`. The set is open, so an amendment may add a profile within v1. Server invariant in v1: the Gateway serves only `gateway-mode-local-v1` and `gateway-mode-air-gapped-v1`.

ModeProfileIdentity.description: The members that identify one GMP1 binding: its kind, profile, mode, digest and store binding epoch. `mode_profile_digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewayModeProfile.v1` || 0x00 || canonical GMP1 bytes), recomputable from `execution-mode-profiles.json`. `mode` pairs with `mode_profile_id`. The schemas that compose it close themselves.

mode.description: The serving mode the profile declares. Open within v1; server invariant: `local` for `gateway-mode-local-v1` and `air-gapped` for `gateway-mode-air-gapped-v1` (the pairing below), and no other mode.

binding_epoch.description: The store binding epoch: 1 at bind, incremented on every rotation and migration.

ModeProfile.description: The GMP1 a resource was produced under. A resource materialized from committed Events or stored revisions reports the binding epoch recorded in its producing commit's evidence; a resource computed per request reports the epoch current when it is computed. The history record of an epoch never changes, so the disclosure stays stable across later rotation or migration. Only Session reports the current mode.

SessionModeProfile.description: The current GMP1 binding of the serving store, with the operator's network grants and this Principal's network posture. `network` is `absent` in Air-Gapped mode; in Local mode it is `capability-granted` only when the GMP1 allows network and the Principal holds the capability `gateway.network.v1`, otherwise `denied`. `gateway.network.v1` authorizes no operation in v1. Clients should show `network_grants` next to `network`, so an operator-exposed spectator or OwnTracks ingress stays visible when the Principal's own network is `denied`.

network_grants.description: The operator's `--network-grant` values, sorted. Open within v1; server invariant: only `owntracks` and `public-read-only` exist, and Air-Gapped accepts none.

network.description: The Principal's network posture: `absent`, `denied` or `capability-granted`. The set is deliberately closed in v1.

ProducedUnderModeProfile.description: One GMP1 binding epoch that covers an exported commit.

binding_epoch.description: The store binding epoch: 1 at bind, incremented on every rotation and migration.

ProvenanceReference.description: The digest of the resource's provenance record and its origin class. Provenance describes lineage only; it is not a signature, conformance or calibration claim.

origin.description: The origin class of the provenance record. The set is deliberately closed in v1.

Availability.description: Capability-filtered availability. Each withheld member names why it is absent, so unknown, unauthorized, revoked, deleted and unavailable stay distinct; an `available` resource withholds nothing.

ResourceEnvelope.description: Every enveloped resource carries its schema identifier, resource ID, exactly one immutable `revision` or monotonic `generation`, provenance, the GMP1 `mode_profile` that produced it (Session reports the current binding), the EPF1-only `execution_profile` and capability-filtered availability. Ordering uses Timeline sequence, Fork generation and schema ordinals, never wall time. An installed execution profile is in the servable set of the resource mode.

revision.description: An immutable revision; a change is a new revision.

generation.description: A monotonic generation; it never decreases.

mode_profile.description: Session reports `session-mode-profile` (the current binding); every other resource reports `mode-profile` (the binding it was produced under).

LifecycleState.description: The resource state machine. No response collapses these states; a resource names the subset it can reach. `submitted` and `rejected` are answered synchronously: a rejection is a problem body.

ReplayClaim.description: The ReplayClaim, strongest first: `exact`, then `exact-authoritative-with-redacted-views` (authoritative Events and Projections still reproduce; some views are redacted), then `structural-only`, then `unverifiable-artifacts-missing`; `incompatible-profile` is orthogonal. Erasure and revocation only preserve or weaken it, so a `degraded` resource never claims `exact`. That a later generation never strengthens the claim is a runtime obligation; a single document cannot show it.

RevisionRef.description: One exact immutable input revision and the digest of its canonical bytes. For a Scenario Room revision the digest is its `provenance.digest`; for a Preference or OptionSpec revision it is its `digest`.

RevisionParent.description: The current head revision of the resource a new revision derives from.

Session.description: The authenticated Principal's own session: its entities, effective grants, consent, the current execution mode (`mode_profile`, with the operator network grants and this Principal's network posture) and the EPF1 execution profile. `id` is the Principal's ID. `generation` is the authority generation: the head position of the Principal's recorded authority chain plus the head of its consent Timeline (0 when its grant binds none), so it advances on every grant, consent or revocation change and never uses wall time. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewaySession.v1` || 0x00 || the 16 bytes of the 128-bit big-endian value of `id` decoded as a Crockford base32 ULID || `generation` as a big-endian u64 || the ASCII `mode_profile.mode_profile_digest` || `mode_profile.binding_epoch` as a big-endian u64), and its origin is `host-derived`. The digest covers the Principal, the generation, the mode digest and the epoch only: the entities, grants and network grants move with the authority head and the binding epoch. `contract.contract_version` is currently `1.0.0-draft`; the schema also accepts `1.0.0`.

grants.description: The names of the operations and capabilities the Principal's recorded grant covers for the acting entity, sorted, as the host's own authority evaluator decides them; a client never supplies a trusted capability. The DomainKey `gateway.network.v1` is the Principal network capability: it authorizes no operation in v1 and only decides the `mode_profile.network` disclosure; it is granted only through explicit-grant provisioning, never an operator flag. A listed name means the grant covers that capability, not that the operation will succeed: the operation may still be refused for its own reasons.

consent_ref.description: The EventId (ULID) of the consent's `consent.granted.v1` Event.

contract_version.description: The Gateway currently returns `1.0.0-draft`; the schema also accepts `1.0.0`.

ScenarioRoomInput.description: The participant-authored members of one ScenarioRoomDescriptor. Unknown members are rejected; the room ID, revision, correlation ID and hashes are server-owned and cannot be supplied. The server admits the lists sorted (plugins by `plugin_id`, rules by `rule_id`, participants by `entity_id`, initial conditions by `entity_id` then `dimension`) and refuses a duplicate key, a `plugin_id` containing `.`, a `rule_id` whose first `.`-separated segment names no requested plugin, and an initial condition whose `entity_id` is not a participant. Every plugin must be bundled by the deployment at exactly its `version`. The canonical descriptor is at most 4,096 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.room_descriptor_bytes`), measured on the admitted `room.revision.v1` payload.

plugins.description: Plugins already admitted and bundled by the deployment trust policy; a room cannot discover, install or retrieve a Plugin.

value_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.
A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

DeriveScenarioRoomRevisionRequest.description: A complete new descriptor derived from `parent_revision`; there is no automatic merge.

ScenarioRoomDescriptor.description: The payload of one `room.revision.v1` Event, encoded as the RFC 8785 bytes of this object. `rule_set_hash` is BLAKE3 of the canonical JSON rules array. `descriptor_hash` is BLAKE3 of the canonical descriptor object before that hash is added. A client can recompute both values; `plugin_composition_hash` is derived from the host catalogue.

plugins.description: Plugins already admitted and bundled by the deployment trust policy; a room cannot discover, install or retrieve a Plugin.

value_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.
A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

correlation_id.description: 16 runtime-generated non-zero bytes; never caller supplied.

ScenarioRoomRevision.description: One immutable Scenario Room revision. `id` is the room ID; `commit` is the `room.revision.v1` Event that recorded it. Every accepted derive appends a new revision, even when its content equals the head, because `descriptor_hash` covers the room ID and revision number. An exact `Idempotency-Key` retry returns the same response. A stale derive whose `parent_revision` is no longer the head returns the existing revision with `200` when its descriptor matches the revision already derived from that parent. Other stale derives return `409 append-conflict`. `provenance.origin` is `principal-authored`, and `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewayScenarioRoomRevision.v1` || 0x00 || the 32 bytes of `descriptor.descriptor_hash` decoded from hex || the 16 bytes of the 128-bit big-endian value of `commit.event_id` decoded as a Crockford base32 ULID), in lower-case hex.

CreatePreferenceRequest.description: Without `parent` it creates revision 1 of a new Preference; with `parent` it creates the next revision of that Preference, whose current head `parent` must name (`409 append-conflict` otherwise). The subject is the acting entity (`x-piglor-actor-entity`), which the Local Principal's grant must cover; a parent of another subject is `404 not-found-or-unavailable`. Identical content is never deduplicated: a retry is recognized only by its `Idempotency-Key`.

schema_version.description: The schema version of the request; any other version is `400 unsupported-version`.

weights.description: Named dimension weights in [-1, 1] as integer micro-units; a dimension appears once (checked at admission). They are a set: the revision answers them ordered by `dimension`.

PreferenceRevision.description: One immutable subject-scoped Preference revision, answered only to its subject: any other caller gets the same `404 not-found-or-unavailable` as for an unknown revision. A revision its subject erased answers `410 deleted` to that subject from a payload-free tombstone and `404 not-found-or-unavailable` to everyone else; no erased value is reconstructed. `provenance.origin` is `principal-authored`, and `mode_profile` is the binding the producing commit recorded. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3 of `PiglorOS.GatewayRevisionProvenance.v1`, a 0x00 byte and the deterministic CBOR array `[origin, principal_id, subject_entity_id, mode_profile_id, mode_profile_digest, binding_epoch, digest]` (text, ULIDs and lower-case hex digests, `binding_epoch` an unsigned integer): the authoring Principal (`Session.principal.principal_id`) and the execution-mode binding the producing commit recorded.

schema_version.description: The schema version the revision was created under.

subject_entity_id.description: The subject the revision is scoped to: the acting entity that created it.

weights.description: Named dimension weights in [-1, 1] as integer micro-units, ordered by `dimension`.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the ASCII domain tag `PiglorOS.GatewayPreferenceRevision.v1` followed by a 0x00 byte and the revision's canonical bytes: the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deterministic CBOR array `[schema_id, schema_version, id, revision, parent_revision, subject_entity_id, weights]` (IDs as canonical ULID text, `parent_revision` null for revision 1), where each weight is `[dimension, weight_micro]`, ordered by `dimension`. A `revision-ref` names a revision by its `id`, `revision` and this digest.

schema_version.description: The schema version of the request; any other version is `400 unsupported-version`.

tags.description: A set of keys; the revision answers them in byte order.

x_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

z_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

options.description: The user-supplied alternatives, in the order the revision keeps; a key appears once (checked at admission). A label is at most 128 UTF-8 bytes (`x-pigloros-limits.label_bytes`).

CreateOptionSpecRequest.description: Without `parent` it creates revision 1 of a new OptionSpec; with `parent` the next revision, whose current head `parent` must name (`409 append-conflict` otherwise). The subject is the acting entity, as for a Preference. Identical content is never deduplicated.

OptionSpecRevision.description: One immutable subject-scoped OptionSpec revision, answered only to its subject: any other caller gets the same `404 not-found-or-unavailable` as for an unknown revision. A revision its subject erased answers `410 deleted` to that subject from a payload-free tombstone and `404 not-found-or-unavailable` to everyone else; no erased value is reconstructed. `provenance.origin` is `principal-authored`, and `mode_profile` is the binding the producing commit recorded. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3 of `PiglorOS.GatewayRevisionProvenance.v1`, a 0x00 byte and the deterministic CBOR array `[origin, principal_id, subject_entity_id, mode_profile_id, mode_profile_digest, binding_epoch, digest]` (text, ULIDs and lower-case hex digests, `binding_epoch` an unsigned integer): the authoring Principal (`Session.principal.principal_id`) and the execution-mode binding the producing commit recorded.

schema_version.description: The schema version the revision was created under.

subject_entity_id.description: The subject the revision is scoped to: the acting entity that created it.

x_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

z_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

options.description: The user-supplied alternatives in their authored order, each with its tags in byte order.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the ASCII domain tag `PiglorOS.GatewayOptionSpecRevision.v1` followed by a 0x00 byte and the revision's canonical bytes: the RFC 8949 §4.2.1 deterministic CBOR array `[schema_id, schema_version, id, revision, parent_revision, subject_entity_id, options]` (IDs as canonical ULID text, `parent_revision` null for revision 1), where each option is `[key, label, tags, lean_hint_micro, coordinates]` in revision order, with `tags` in byte order, `lean_hint_micro` null when absent and `coordinates` the array `[x_micro, z_micro]` or null. A `revision-ref` names a revision by its `id`, `revision` and this digest.

CreateDecisionPreviewRequest.description: Binds one inert preview to exact input revisions and one execution profile. `scenario_room.digest` is the room revision's `provenance.digest`, not its `descriptor_hash`; `preference` and `option_spec` name the revisions by their `digest`.

schema_version.description: The schema version of the request; any other number is `400 unsupported-version`, and a value that is not a number is `400 invalid-request`.

DecisionPreview.description: One Decision Preview. Admission (`admitted`) is never a commit claim; only `committed` names an Event sequence. `committed` is null exactly while the preview is `admitted` or `failed` (pre-commit); every later state, including `degraded`, follows a commit. `committed` names the preview's `preview.result.v1` Event; simulated actions are referenced by their own member. `failure` is an object exactly when the state is `failed`. Uncertainty and calibration are separate members and never stand in for the Recommendation's evidence. Every proposal is inert and no route creates a real-world effect.

toss_up.description: True when `margin_micro` < 20,000 (0.02 on the signed scale); `option_key` is then null.

margin_micro.description: The largest score minus the second-largest (max minus second-max); 0 when the maximum is shared.

scores.description: Every option once, in the OptionSpec's authored order, scored by `pigloros.match-score.v1`.

oneOf.description: A `degraded` preview: a bound input was erased, so no value derived from it is shown.

committed.description: The preview's `preview.result.v1` Event, once its result committed; null while `admitted` or `failed`. Its `next_cursor` is null: no client reads the `decision-previews` Timeline.

code.description: The typed terminal failure. Open within v1. `input-deleted` is the only typed terminal failure code produced for a Decision Preview.

failure.description: The typed terminal failure of a `failed` preview; null in every other state.

SimulatedActionRequest.description: One typed simulated ProposedAction of the preview's factual Timeline. It is authorized, approved by the host-owned ActionApprover and only then committed; it mutates simulation state only. The canonical payload is at most 4,096 bytes.

observed_seq.description: The Logical Head the client observed; a moved head is `append-conflict`.

ProjectionView.description: One page of a capability-filtered Projection at a Projection Cut. `id` is the Timeline ID and `generation` its Fork generation (0 for a factual Timeline); a quarantined generation is never served.

fold_cursor.description: The Projection Cut: the last sequence folded.

value.description: The capability-filtered state value; absent when withheld.

Intervention.description: One ordered Intervention. Ordinals are contiguous from 0; an Intervention cannot target consent, capability, trust, erasure or audit state.

value_micro.description: A value in integer micro-units (10^-6) for deterministic Replay.

forks.description: Ordered Forks; at least one is the explicitly labelled adversarial condition.

Ensemble.description: An ordered ensemble of generation-isolated Forks with complete endogenous suffix recomputation. A Fork that is not `complete` exposes no suffix digest: no partial suffix is authoritative, and an `incomplete` Fork names its failure. A `complete` ensemble has only complete Forks. Fork ordinals are unique and contiguous from 0 in array order; JSON Schema cannot express that, so the contract check enforces it on every example.

CreateReplayRequest.description: Replays one named immutable closure. A closure whose ReplayClaim is weaker than `minimum_replay_claim` is `replay-claim-insufficient`.

Replay.description: One Replay: the execution-profile class and outcome with its ReplayClaim, an independent tuple. A computational match never strengthens the claim. `verified-exact` with `exact-authoritative-with-redacted-views` is coherent (the authoritative outputs matched; views are redacted), but `verified-exact` is impossible once only structural or no artifact evidence remains or the profile is incompatible. A `degraded` Replay never claims `exact`.

Uncertainty.description: Uncertainty of a result: explicitly `unavailable` or `insufficient-evidence`, otherwise `reported` with its method, ensemble size and spread. It never stands in for calibration.

CalibrationStatus.description: Calibration Report status: explicitly `unavailable` or `insufficient-evidence`, otherwise a report naming its population, method and limitations. It is named empirical evidence, never general truth.

PreviewEvidence.description: Reactions, trace, uncertainty, Calibration Report status, provenance and claim strength of one preview. Evidence classes are separate members and never substitute for one another; Plugin metadata is digest-bound disclosure without Plugin authority.

reactions.description: Committed reactions in Timeline Order; `fork_ordinal` is null on the factual Timeline.

trace.description: The structured trace page, ordered by `ordinal`.

external_copy_acknowledged.description: The subject acknowledges that an authorized copy outside PiglorOS cannot be recalled.

Export.description: A minimized, content-addressed, subject-authorized export and its ReproManifest closure, paged by `next_cursor`. An `exported` export names its ReproManifest. Later erasure redacts managed records and weakens the ReplayClaim (a `degraded` export never claims `exact`); it does not claim that external copies vanished. `produced_under_mode_profiles` lists the GMP1 binding epochs its commits were produced under.

produced_under_mode_profiles.description: Every GMP1 binding epoch that covers an exported commit, sorted by `binding_epoch`. The source deployment's produced-under modes travel here; an importing store records them under its own importing epoch and does not re-assert them.

ConsentRevocation.description: A recorded consent revocation. `id` is the `EventId` of its `consent.revoked.v1` Event and `generation` is its sequence on the Principal's consent Timeline, from which the revocation is effective. It is the consent fence, not the `Session` authority generation. A `Session` read at or after the revocation reports `generation` greater than or equal to it. The revocation stops future protected work governed by the consent and is distinct from erasure. `provenance.digest` is BLAKE3(UTF-8 `PiglorOS.GatewayConsentRevocation.v1` || 0x00 || the 16 bytes of the 128-bit big-endian value of the Principal's ID (its `Session` `id`) decoded as a Crockford base32 ULID || `generation` as a big-endian u64 || the ASCII `mode_profile.mode_profile_digest` || `mode_profile.binding_epoch` as a big-endian u64), and its origin is `host-derived`. `mode_profile` is the binding recorded by the revocation commit, so every answer about that revocation is stable.

ErasureRequest.description: One erasure request. `scope` is one scope class; a Local deployment destroys `private-subject-data` and `consented-shared-data` and always retains the other three, which it refuses with `erasure-scope-retained`.

impact_acknowledged.description: The subject saw the retained classes and the ReplayClaim impact.

Erasure.description: The authenticated subject's own erasure. `state` is the lifecycle of its verified ERS1 head; `generation` is the head's ERS1 ordinal times 2^16 plus the acknowledgements committed in the active attempt; every attempt closes with a new ERS1 state, so it never decreases; `provenance.digest` is the raw ERS1 state digest; `redaction_generation` is the store-wide count of committed client-cache redaction generations, which never decreases; `mode_profile` is the execution-mode binding the erasure was submitted under. `acknowledgements.required` counts the frozen obligations (0 before the access freeze) and `positive` the positive acknowledgements of the effective inventory, also per acknowledgement class in `classes`. The erasure lifecycle is monotonic, a `complete` erasure has as many positive acknowledgements as required, destroyed values are never reconstructed and the ReplayClaim never strengthens: these are runtime obligations that a single document cannot show, not schema rules.

state.description: The erasure lifecycle; no edge is backward.

scope.description: The scope class the request names; only a destruction-eligible class is ever admitted.

classes.description: The same counts per acknowledgement class, in class order; empty before the access freeze. A class is an open pattern string: a client handles a class it does not know.

redaction_generation.description: The store-wide count of committed client-cache redaction generations across all subjects and erasures. It never decreases and starts at zero. A Gateway with a Local erasure composition includes it. Clients compare it with the last value they saw and re-read before trusting a cached copy when it increases.

PageCursor.name: cursor
PageCursor.description: Continuation from the previous page's cursor.

Problem.description: A failure of the problem-types.json registry.

CacheControl.description: Every Gateway response, including problem responses, carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

label_bytes.source: pos-crypto plugin_manifest MAX_LABEL_BYTES; UTF-8 bytes checked at admission, Label maxLength is only the coarse character bound

decision_previews_per_store.source: Half of events_per_timeline, with two Events per preview
